# Logistic Regression on Body Data 
```{r}
z <- read.table("/Users/sorenbasnet/Desktop/STAT_443_SP_2026/Data_files_export/bodydata.txt",header=TRUE)
tmp <- rep(0,nrow(z))
tmp[z$Gender == "M"] <- 1
z$Gender <- tmp
logit <- glm(Gender ~ .,data=z,family=binomial)
prob <- predict(logit,data=z,type='response')
predicted <- ifelse(prob > 0.5,"M","F")
table(predicted,z$Gender)
```






```{r}
summary(logit)

```


Remark : Quasi-complete separation occurs when predictors almost perfectly classify the response, causing the logistic regression likelihood to increase without bound and resulting in extremely large coefficient estimates, inflated standard errors, near-zero residual deviance, and invalid Wald inference.
